0.172 g of an organic compound showed
presence of 0.08 g of bromine. Which of these
is the correct structure of the compound?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In Carius method

mass of organic compound = 0.172 gm

mass of Bromine = 0.08 gm

Hence % of Bromine = $\frac{0.08}{0.172}\times 100$

= 46.51 %

Option (A) Br mass % = $\frac{80}{109}\times 100$ = 73.33%

(B) Br mass % = $\frac{80}{95}\times 100$ = 84.2 %

(C) Br mass % = $\frac{80}{172}\times 100$ = 46.51 %

(D) Br mass % = $\frac{80\times 2}{252}\times 100$ = 63.49 %

text:
If $AB_{4}$ molecule is a polar molecule, a possible
geometry of $AB_{4}$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
An $\mathrm{AB}{}_{4}$ molecule is polar only if its four A–B bond dipoles do not cancel.

Tetrahedral: the four equal A–B dipoles point to the corners of a regular tetrahedron and cancel, so the molecule is non-polar (e.g. $\mathrm{CH}{}_{4}$, $\mathrm{CCl}{}_{4}$).

Rectangular planar and square planar: every A–B dipole has an equal one pointing the opposite way (at $180^{\circ }$), so they cancel and both shapes are non-polar (e.g. $\mathrm{XeF}{}_{4}$ is square planar).

Square pyramidal: A sits at the apex above the square of four B atoms. The components of the four dipoles in the plane of the base cancel, but their components along the axis all point the same way and add up, so the molecule has a net dipole moment and is polar.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Morning Slot

text:
For the following Assertion and Reason, the
correct option is

Assertion (A): When Cu (II) and sulphide ions
are mixed, they react together
extremely quickly to give a
solid.

Reason (R): The equilibrium constant of

$Cu^{2+}(aq) + S^{2–}(aq)$ ⇌ CuS(s) is
high because the solubility
product is low.
options:
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the
explanation for (A).

Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the
explanation for (A).
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The precipitation $\mathrm{Cu}{}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq})+\mathrm{S}{}^{2-}(\mathrm{aq})\longrightarrow \mathrm{CuS}(\mathrm{s})$ is an ionic reaction that occurs at once on mixing, so the assertion is true.

For this reaction $K=\dfrac{1}{K_{\text{sp}}(\mathrm{CuS})}$, and $K_{\text{sp}}$ is of the order of $10^{-36}$, so $K$ is very large and the reason is true.

An equilibrium constant measures how far a reaction proceeds, not how fast it proceeds; $2~\mathrm{H}{}_{2}+\mathrm{O}{}_{2}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$, for example, has a very large $K$ yet is extremely slow at room temperature, so the reason does not explain the speed stated in the assertion.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Morning Slot

[IMG]


'x', 'y' and 'z' in these reactions are respectively.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(i) With ROH and dry HCl, the anomeric C-1 OH of glucose becomes OR, giving the glycoside (acetal). Four free OH groups remain (C-2, C-3, C-4 and C-6), so 4 equivalents of $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CO}){}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ are used: $x=4$.

(ii) $\mathrm{Ni}/\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$ reduces the CHO group to $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}$, giving sorbitol, $\mathrm{HOCH}{}_{2}(\mathrm{CHOH}){}_{4}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}$, with six OH groups: $y=6$.

(iii) Glucose has five OH groups and forms glucose pentaacetate: $z=5$.

So $x$, $y$ and $z$ are 4, 6 and 5 respectively.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
For octahedral Mn(II) and tetrahedral Ni(II)
complexes, consider the following statements:

(I) both the complexes can be high spin.

(II) Ni(II) complex can very rarely be low spin.

(III) with strong field ligands, Mn(II) complexes
can be low spin.

(IV) aqueous solution of Mn(II) ions is yellow in
colour.

The correct statements are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Octahedral Mn(II) is $d^{5}$. With weak-field ligands ($\Delta _{o}<P$) the configuration is $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{2}$ with 5 unpaired electrons (high spin), as in $[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{2+}$. With strong-field ligands such as $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ ($\Delta _{o}>P$) the electrons pair in $t_{2g}$, giving $t_{2g}^{5}e_{g}^{0}$ with 1 unpaired electron (low spin), as in $[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{4-}$. So (III) is correct.

Tetrahedral Ni(II) is $d^{8}$, $e^{4}t_{2}^{4}$ with 2 unpaired electrons (high spin), as in $[\mathrm{NiCl}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}$. Both complexes can therefore be high spin, so (I) is correct.

The tetrahedral splitting is small ($\Delta _{t}\approx \dfrac{4}{9}\Delta _{o}$) and is almost never larger than the pairing energy, so tetrahedral Ni(II) complexes are very rarely low spin; diamagnetic Ni(II) complexes are square planar instead. So (II) is correct.

Aqueous $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{2+}$, present as $[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{2+}$, is pale pink, not yellow, so (IV) is incorrect.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Morning Slot

text:
Consider that $a d^{6}$ metal ion $(M^{2+})$ forms a
complex with aqua ligands, and the spin only
magnetic moment of the complex is 4.90 BM.
The geometry and the crystal field stabilization
energy of the complex is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A spin-only moment of $4.90\text{BM}$ gives $\sqrt{n(n+2)}=4.90\Rightarrow n=4$ unpaired electrons, so the $d^{6}$ ion is high spin.

In an octahedral field, high-spin $d^{6}$ is $t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{2}$ with CFSE $=4(-0.4\Delta _{o})+2(0.6\Delta _{o})=-0.4\Delta _{o}$, which matches neither octahedral option; $-2.4\Delta _{o}+2P$ is low-spin $t_{2g}^{6}$ with no unpaired electron.

In a tetrahedral field, $d^{6}$ is $e^{3}t_{2}^{3}$ with 4 unpaired electrons and CFSE $=3(-0.6\Delta _{t})+3(0.4\Delta _{t})=-0.6\Delta _{t}$, with no pairing beyond that of the free ion; $-1.6\Delta _{t}+P$ is the $e^{4}t_{2}^{2}$ arrangement with only 2 unpaired electrons.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Morning Slot

text:
Which of the following compounds will show
retention in configuration on nucleophilic
substitution by $OH^{–}$ ion?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Configuration is retained when no bond to the stereocentre is broken during the substitution.

In (C), $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5})-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{Br}$, the stereocentre is C-2, while $\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}$ displaces $\mathrm{Br}{}^{-}$ at the primary carbon C-1 ($\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$). No bond to C-2 is broken, so the product $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5})-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}$ keeps the same configuration.


[IMG]

In (A) and (D), Br is on the stereocentre itself, so substitution gives inversion ($\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$) or racemisation ($\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$); (B), 2-bromopropane, has no stereocentre, so neither retention nor inversion can be observed.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
In general the property (magnitudes only) that
show an opposite trend in comparison to other
properties across a period is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Across a period (left to right) in the periodic table :

Ionization enthalpy tends to increase  

Electron gain enthalpy (in magnitude) tends to increase (more negative values)  

Electronegativity tends to increase  

Atomic radius tends to decrease  

Hence, atomic radius shows the opposite trend compared to the other three properties. Therefore, the correct answer is

(D) Atomic radius.

text:
The oxidation states of iron atoms in
compounds (A), (B) and (C), respectively, are x,
y and z. The sum of x, y and z is $________$.

$Na_{4}$[$Fe(CN)_{5}($NOS)]

       (A)

$Na_{4}$[FeO$_{4}$]

       (B)

[$Fe_{2}(CO)_{9}$]

       (C)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $\mathrm{Na}{}_{4}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{5}(\mathrm{NOS})]$ the complex ion forms from nitroprusside and sulfide, $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{5}\mathrm{NO}]{}^{2-}+\mathrm{S}{}^{2-}\longrightarrow [\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{5}(\mathrm{NOS})]{}^{4-}$; iron keeps its +2 state and $\mathrm{NOS}$ ($\mathrm{NO}{}^{+}$ combined with $\mathrm{S}{}^{2-}$) carries a charge of $-1$.

$4(+1)+x+5(-1)+(-1)=0\Rightarrow x=+2$

In $\mathrm{Na}{}_{4}[\mathrm{FeO}{}_{4}]$: $4(+1)+y+4(-2)=0\Rightarrow y=+4$.

In $[\mathrm{Fe}{}_{2}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{9}]$, CO is a neutral ligand: $2z+9(0)=0\Rightarrow z=0$.

$x+y+z=2+4+0=6$

Hence, the answer is 6.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Morning Slot

text:
The internal energy change (in J) When 90 g of
water undergoes complete evaporation at
$100^{o}C$ is $____________$.

(Given : $\DeltaH_{$vap} for water at 373 K = 41 kJ/mol,

$R = 8.314 JK^{–1}$ mol$^{–1})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$H_{2}O(l)$ ⇌ $H_{2}O(g)$

90 gm of $H_{2}O =$ $\frac{90}{18}$ moles of $H_{2}O = 5$ moles of $H_{2}O$

$\DeltaH_{$vap} = $\Delta$U + $\Deltan_{g}RT$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta$U = $\DeltaH_{$vap} - $\Deltan_{g}RT$

= 41000 - 1$\times$8.314$\times$373

= 37898.878

For 5 moles, $\Delta$U = 37898.878 $\times$ 5 = 189494.39 Joule
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Morning Slot
